title: Day-of Timeline and Run of Show
subtitle: Sample run-of-show schedules for a party, a wedding, and a corporate evening, plus load-in, emergency, and contact sheets.
intro: A run of show is the minute-by-minute script that keeps your vendors, helpers, and guests moving in the same direction. Use the samples as a starting point, change the times to fit your event, and hand a copy to every vendor. The checklists and contact sheet make sure nobody is guessing on the big day.

sections.heading: How to Use a Run of Show
items: Work backward from the event start time and the venue curfew, then fill in the rest.
Add 10 to 15 minute buffers around meals, speeches, and anything involving a crowd.
List who is responsible for each item so no moment is left without an owner.
Send the final version to every vendor at least two weeks before the event and again the day before.
Print one copy for the host, one for the day-of coordinator, one for the DJ or emcee, and one for the caterer.
Use the same clock for everyone. Agree on whose phone or watch is the official time.
Build in a plan B for weather, late vendors, and running behind. Decide in advance what gets cut first.
Tape a short version of the schedule where vendors can see it in the back of the house.

sections.heading: Sample: 4-Hour Party Run of Show
sections.note: Example for a 6:00 pm to 10:00 pm birthday, anniversary, or graduation party with a seated or buffet dinner. Adjust all times.
rows: Rental delivery: tables, chairs, linens, tent if needed
Host or helper receives and inspects
Caterer and bartender arrive and set up
Decor, signage, and seating display go up
DJ or musician arrives, sound check
Final walk-through and photo of the setup
Host and family ready, staff in position
Doors open, welcome drinks and appetizers
Last call and cake to go
Send-off, thank guests, hand out favors
Rentals stacked or packed, trash out, venue cleared

sections.heading: Sample: Wedding Day Run of Show
sections.note: Example for a 4:00 pm ceremony and an evening reception. Shift everything to match your actual start time.
rows: Florist delivers bouquets, boutonnieres, and arch pieces
Rental delivery: ceremony chairs, reception tables, linens, lighting
Light lunch for the wedding party
Maid of honor or best man
DJ or band arrives and sets up
Ceremony musicians arrive, final décor check
Guests begin to arrive, ushers seat guests
Wedding party and couple photos continue
Best man, maid of honor, caterer
Late-night snack, bouquet or garter moments if wanted
Venue empty, rentals ready for pickup

sections.heading: Sample: Corporate Evening Event Run of Show
sections.note: Example for a 5:30 pm to 9:30 pm awards dinner or client reception.
rows: Rental delivery: tables, chairs, linens, stage, lighting
Decor, signage, and registration table setup
Tech rehearsal with the presenter or emcee
Venue cleared, rentals counted and stacked

groups.title: Before vendors arrive
items: Confirm the venue load-in time, loading dock, and elevator rules in writing.
Reserve parking or a loading zone for delivery trucks.
Unlock doors, turn on lights, and set the thermostat before the first vendor arrives.
Clear the space of existing furniture and storage items.
Make sure restrooms and water access are available to vendors.
Post a sign or send a map showing where each vendor should unload.

groups.title: Rental delivery
items: Have a floor plan on site so the driver knows where each table and chair set goes.
Count tables, chairs, linens, plates, glasses, and flatware against the order.
Check for stains, tears, cracks, and missing items before signing.
Take photos of any damage and note it on the delivery slip.
Confirm the pickup time and where items should be stacked.
Put tips for the delivery crew in a labeled envelope.

groups.title: Food and beverage
items: Show the caterer the kitchen, power outlets, and sinks.
Confirm where hot boxes, coolers, and ice will be stored.
Give the bartender the bar location and the signature drink list.
Make sure licensed alcohol service is in place and permits are visible.
Plan a staff meal for caterers and vendors who work more than five hours.

groups.title: Entertainment, photo, and decor
items: Give the DJ or band power access, a table, and a clear load-in path.
Tell the photographer the schedule, must-have shots, and family groupings.
Introduce the florist to the person who will approve placement.
Confirm the officiant, emcee, or speakers know their cues.
Keep a list of who has arrived, who is late, and who has left.

sections.heading: Day-of Emergency Kit
sections.note: Pack in a bin and hand it to your day-of coordinator.

groups.title: Repairs and tools
items: Scissors, tape, fishing line, and double-sided tape.
Safety pins, sewing kit, and fabric glue.
Zip ties, clips, and wire.
Steamer or wrinkle spray for linens.
Extension cords, power strip, and spare batteries.
Flashlight and a headlamp for dark setup.

groups.title: Health and comfort
items: First aid kit, bandages, and pain relievers.
Antacids, tissues, and allergy medicine.
Sunscreen and bug spray.
Umbrellas, ponchos, blankets, and hand warmers for cold Chicago nights.
Water bottles, granola bars, and a cooler of cold drinks.
Spare shoes, flip-flops, or blister bandages.

groups.title: Paper and money
items: Master run of show and the contact sheet.
Copies of vendor contracts and permits.
Envelopes with tips and final payments.
Cash for parking and small purchases.
Pens, markers, and blank cards.
Garbage bags, cleaning wipes, and paper towels.

sections.heading: Day-of Contact Sheet
sections.note: Fill this in, make four copies, and share with your coordinator, host, and key helpers.
fields: DJ or band lead and cell

sections.heading: Questions to Ask Before the Day
items: What time can each vendor access the venue, and who unlocks the doors?
Where can vendors park, and do they need passes or permits?
Is there a freight elevator or only stairs?
What is the venue noise curfew, and when must the music end?
Who is authorized to approve changes on the day?
What is the weather backup plan, and who decides when to use it?
Who will collect gifts, cards, and personal items after the event?
What time must the venue be fully cleared and rentals ready for pickup?
